function: Joint end-to-end CAE: neural PAPR-reduction encoder at the transmitter and neural iterative MIMO detector at the receiver recovering QAM symbols after a nonlinear HPA (pp. 13-17).
system: MIMO-OFDM 2x2 QPSK and 4x4 16-QAM, 72 subcarriers, 4x oversampling, RAPP nonlinear HPA per branch, 3GPP TDL-D or AWGN; no RIS; carrier frequency not given (pp. 8-11, 20-21).
method: Convolutional autoencoder: CNN encoder and iterative CNN decoder (10 iterations, learned step sizes), trained end-to-end on known symbols with augmented-Lagrangian multi-loss, gradual loss learning, AdamW (pp. 14-19, 22).
data_channel: MATLAB 5G Toolbox simulated MIMO-OFDM data over 3GPP TDL-D channels (13 taps, 30 ns delay spread) and AWGN; 4375 batches of 32 samples per training set (pp. 20-21).
test_conditions: Separate CAE per setup (2x2 QPSK, 4x4 16-QAM with 3GPP or AWGN), trained at 40 dB; tested on independent data of that setup, 7000 samples per SNR (pp. 21-22).
baselines: Non-learned: CF and SLM with MLE detection, plus no-PAPR-reduction reference. Learned: FC-AE; fixed-loss CAE is a variant (pp. 21, 26-27).
metrics: BER versus peak SNR (P-SNR), PAPR CCDF, PSD, ACPR (dB), output back-off OBO (dB), parameter count (pp. 22-27).
complexity: Parameters only: three convolutional layers total 1953 parameters versus about 10^7 for the FC-AE; no operation counts or runtime (p. 26).
q1_support: p. 20: "TDL-D type channels - a 13 delay tap channel with a 30ns delay spread, as described in the 3gpp specification document [6]"; [6] is 3GPP 38.901 (p. 28). Used for training and test in two of three setups.
q2_support: p. 21: "the training and test data sets were generated independently", same setup for each of three separately trained CAEs; only an SNR sweep varies (Fig. 4). Missing: no new channel, antenna count or modulation at test.
q3_support: p. 21: "compared to a classical CF algorithm with a clipping ratio of 4.08 dB, and to SLM with U = 64 phase sequences, with MLE added for MIMO detection"; p. 26: "the CAE network has better BER performance compared to the FC-AE", a fully connected autoencoder.
q4_support: p. 26: "The three convolutional layers have a total of 1953 parameters", against about 10^7 for the FC-AE (p. 27). Only a parameter count; no FLOPs, order of complexity or runtime.
q5_support: p. 20: "MATLAB® 5G Toolbox™ [46] was used" to generate simulated data. Missing: no code or data link or DOI anywhere, and the toolbox is not a public channel dataset.
notes: Included on function: the learned decoder is a neural iterative MIMO detector (pp. 13-17) and BER is the key metric (p. 22); PAPR reduction alone would be excluded, so the reviewer should confirm that the joint task passes. Area 1. q3 counts the FC-AE as the standard fully connected baseline (p. 26); no earlier learned detector is compared although refs [10]-[13] are cited (pp. 4-5). q4 rests on the parameter count of three convolutional layers, consistent with the three 1x3 encoder layers of Table I (p. 22); no FLOPs or runtime. q1 holds for two of three setups, the third being AWGN (p. 21).
